data.title: Merge
data.tagline: Combine the commits from one branch into another
data.description: Merge brings two lines of history together. Git can combine independent changes automatically, but overlapping edits may create conflicts that a person must resolve. Review the result and run tests after resolving, because a clean text merge can still break behavior.

use: Bring a reviewed feature into main
avoid: Resolve a conflict without understanding both sides
Merge into the wrong target branch
Assume no text conflict means no product conflict
Mix unrelated cleanup into conflict resolution

explanation.title: Git merge vs rebase: which should you use?
explanation.text: Use Merge as the safer default for shared commits. Consider Rebase on an unshared personal branch when you want a linear history before review. Commit history: Git Merge — Preserves true branch history and explicit merge commits (or fast-forwards the branch pointer).; Git Rebase — Replays commits onto a new base, generating new commit hashes to produce a linear history.. Collaboration: Git Merge — Keeps existing commit IDs, making shared history easier to integrate.; Git Rebase — Creates new commit IDs; rewriting shared history requires explicit team coordination.. When to use: Git Merge — Merging a feature into main or integrating a shared team branch.; Git Rebase — Cleaning up an unshared personal branch or replaying it onto the latest main before review.. A feature branch with active collaborators: When teammates have already based work on your branch, Merge is the safer default because it does not rewrite commits they pulled. If the branch has not been shared, Rebase can place it on the latest main before review. Rewriting shared history should follow an explicit team agreement.

lessonPractice.title: A feature branch is ready for main, but both sides changed one line. What is the reliable conflict handling?

options.label: Understand both intents, produce the correct combined content, clear markers, and run relevant tests
options.feedback: Correct. A conflict is not a choice of a side; retain the right behavior and verify it still runs.

options.label: Always choose the current branch because it is closest to your work
options.feedback: It may omit a required fix from the target branch.

options.label: Commit the conflict markers and let CI decide later
options.feedback: Conflict markers are not runnable code and need an explicit resolution first.

data.agentPrompt: Merge this feature branch into its target. First inspect what each side must preserve, resolve the conflict, confirm no markers remain, and run relevant tests. Report the merge and test results; do not resolve it by arbitrarily choosing one side.
